standard.title: Superannuation system
standard.description: the importance of Australia's superannuation system and how this system affects consumer and financial decision-making
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand factors that influence major consumer and financial decisions and their short- and long-term consequences (AC9HE10K03). They can analyse how financial commitments accumulate over time and consider the role of savings. Students have also explored how governments redistribute income through transfers and services (AC9HE10K02).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain the importance of Australia's superannuation system for individual retirement wellbeing and government fiscal sustainability, and explain how the system shapes consumer and financial decision-making.

nodes.label: What superannuation is and why it exists
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain what superannuation is, why Australia introduced a compulsory super system, and the dual purpose it serves for individuals and government.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain what superannuation is and state at least two reasons why Australia has a compulsory superannuation system.
nodes.typical_width: Explain the importance of Australia's superannuation system in relation to human and financial wellbeing in retirement, and explain why the system also serves the government's ability to maintain a welfare payment system — reducing future pension dependency.
wider: Investigate how Australia's superannuation system compares internationally — examining countries with defined benefit vs accumulation models and what trade-offs each involves
Analyse the history of superannuation in Australia — why it was introduced in the 1990s, at what rate, and how it has evolved to today's rate
Examine how the ageing population creates pressure on government welfare payments and evaluate how superannuation is intended to reduce this pressure
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who see superannuation only as savings for retirement — without understanding the government's fiscal rationale — cannot explain the system's design features (compulsion, tax treatment, preservation rules). The dual rationale is foundational.

response_modes.reason: Build both rationales explicitly: individual retirement income security AND reduced government pension liability. Students commonly grasp the individual rationale but miss the systemic one. The systemic rationale explains compulsion and tax incentives.

success_criteria: Explains what superannuation is in terms of how it works (regular contributions, investment, access at retirement)
States both the individual wellbeing and government fiscal rationale for compulsory super

nodes.label: How a super fund works
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how an individual superannuation fund operates — who contributes, how it is taxed, and how the fund grows over time.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify who contributes to a superannuation fund and explain at least one tax feature of the system.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how individuals manage a personal superannuation fund: who contributes (employer, employee, government co-contribution), how contributions are taxed, how to consolidate funds, how to find lost super, and how to track account performance.
wider: Model the compound growth of a superannuation account over a working life, varying contribution rates and investment options to show the effect of early vs late contributions
Investigate the implications of employment gaps (e.g. career breaks, casual work, unpaid care) on superannuation balance at retirement and who is most affected
Examine the gender superannuation gap — why women retire with significantly less super than men — and evaluate policy responses

response_modes.reason: Vary the worked examples — different employment types, contribution levels, and life stages — so students understand that super outcomes vary significantly depending on individual circumstances.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The gender super gap, employment gap effects and compound growth modelling are rich, real and directly relevant to Year 10 students' futures. These directions produce genuine financial literacy beyond the descriptor's minimum.
success_criteria: Identifies employer and employee as contributors and describes the employer's compulsory obligation
Explains at least one tax feature of superannuation (e.g. concessional tax on contributions or earnings)

nodes.label: Super investment decisions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain why individuals make decisions about superannuation investment options and how personal circumstances affect these decisions.
nodes.minimum_width: State at least two factors related to personal circumstances that might influence which super investment option a person chooses (e.g. age, employment status).
nodes.typical_width: Explain why individuals choose different superannuation investment options (growth, balanced, conservative, ethical) based on circumstances including age, employment status, number of dependants, and anticipated retirement age; explain the relationship between investment risk and likely return over time.
wider: Investigate the growth of ethical and ESG (environmental, social, governance) superannuation options and evaluate whether ethical investing compromises returns
Analyse how investment option selection changes across a working life — why a 25-year-old and a 60-year-old should typically choose differently — using the concept of investment horizon
Compare how self-managed super funds (SMSFs) differ from industry and retail funds and evaluate the circumstances in which an SMSF might be appropriate

response_modes.reason: Different personal profiles (young casual worker, mid-career professional, near-retirement worker) illustrate how the same system produces different optimal strategies. Vary the scenario rather than deepening analysis of one profile.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Investment horizon analysis, ethical investment and SMSF structures extend the descriptor meaningfully and are increasingly relevant to students' near-future financial decisions. The variety of investment option types provides rich comparative material.
success_criteria: Names at least two personal circumstance factors that influence investment option choice
Explains the general relationship between investment risk and return, and how this relates to time horizon

nodes.label: Superannuation and broader financial decision-making
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how the existence of superannuation affects other consumer and financial decisions — including career choices, savings behaviour, insurance, and planning for retirement.
nodes.minimum_width: Give one example of how superannuation affects a non-super financial decision (e.g. how super balance affects decisions about additional voluntary contributions or salary sacrifice).
nodes.typical_width: Explain how superannuation shapes broader consumer and financial decision-making — including how people think about retirement income, whether to salary sacrifice, how to balance super with other savings goals, and how employment decisions (e.g. casual vs permanent work) affect super outcomes.
wider: Investigate the interaction between superannuation and the Age Pension means test — how super balance affects eligibility and what this implies for optimal drawdown strategy
Evaluate the financial implications of taking paid vs unpaid parental leave on super and lifetime retirement savings
Examine how superannuation death benefits and estate planning interact, and why beneficiary nominations matter

response_modes.reason: This node integrates the system design, operational mechanics, and investment choices into the broader picture of how super shapes financial decision-making across a working life. It completes the descriptor's second demand — how super affects consumer and financial decision-making.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one way that superannuation influences a financial decision outside of super itself
Explains how employment type (e.g. casual, part-time, permanent) affects superannuation outcomes
